title: Circuits - 123 school
heading: Circuits
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.q: How is an ammeter placed in a circuit?
How is a voltmeter placed in a circuit?
What is Ohm's law?
A current of 0.50 A flows through a resistor of 12 Ω. What is the voltage?
The voltage across a resistor is 9.0 V and the current is 0.30 A. What is the resistance?
A 46 Ω heating element is connected to 230 V. What is the current?
What is the unit of resistance?
What is true for the current in a series circuit?
questions.a: The current is the same everywhere

questions.q: What is true for the voltage in a series circuit?
questions.a: The source voltage is shared between the components

questions.q: What is true for the voltage across components connected in parallel?
questions.a: The voltage across each component is the same

questions.q: What is true for the current in a parallel circuit?
questions.a: The total current is the sum of the currents through the branches

questions.q: What happens to the other lamps if one lamp burns out in a series circuit?
What happens to the other lamps if one lamp burns out in a parallel circuit?
How are the appliances in a house connected?
Two resistors of 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
Three resistors of 8.0 Ω are in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
Two resistors of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance? (1/R<sub>v</sub> = 1/R<sub>1</sub> + 1/R<sub>2</sub>)
Two equal resistors of 20 Ω are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.a: With two equal resistors, R<sub>v</sub> is half: 10 Ω

questions.q: What happens to the equivalent resistance if you connect an extra resistor in parallel?
Two resistors of 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in series on a 12 V source. What is the current?
questions.a: R<sub>v</sub> = 25 Ω; I = U / R<sub>v</sub> = 12 / 25 = 0.48 A

questions.q: The same circuit: 10 Ω and 15 Ω in series on 12 V, current 0.48 A. What is the voltage across the 10 Ω resistor?
A 6.0 Ω resistor and a 12 Ω resistor are in parallel on 12 V. What is the total current?
In a parallel circuit, two ammeters in the branches read 0.30 A and 0.20 A. What is the total current?
In a series circuit, two voltmeters across two lamps read 4.0 V and 2.0 V. What is the source voltage?
You connect two 1.5 V batteries in series. What is the total voltage?
A 6.0 V lamp has a power of 3.0 W. What is the current through the lamp? (P = U × I)
How does the resistance of a thin wire compare with that of a thick wire (same material and length)?
questions.a: The thin wire has a greater resistance

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a wire if you make the wire twice as long?
questions.a: The resistance becomes twice as large

questions.q: What does an NTC do at a higher temperature?
What does an LDR do when more light falls on it?
What do you use a variable resistor for?
questions.a: To control the resistance, and with it the current

questions.q: What happens in a short circuit?
questions.a: A very large current flows because the resistance is very small

questions.q: Three equal resistors of 30 Ω are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.a: With three equal resistors, R<sub>v</sub> is a third: 30 / 3 = 10 Ω

questions.q: Where do you connect a voltmeter to measure the voltage across a lamp?
questions.a: In parallel with the lamp (connected to both sides of the lamp)

questions.q: Name two advantages of a parallel circuit in a house.
questions.a: Every appliance gets the full mains voltage and you can switch appliances on and off separately
